title: Strike Bowl
observed_goal: In the opening frame, the page presents the goal as bowling and attempting to score over 5 frames; in active-game frames, the ball is seen on the lane and then near the pins. A win, loss, or game completion was not observed.
observed_controls: The page text introduces Space for Bowl; acceptance of this input was not independently confirmed.
The page text introduces A/D for movement and Mouse for aiming; the independent result of these inputs cannot be attributed with certainty from the frames.
The page text introduces holding click or Space for power and horizontal dragging for hook; these are page instructions, not definitively playtested controls.
observed_core_loop: Direct evidence covers only part of the loop: frame 1/5 and Ball 1 are displayed, the ball is seen on the lane, and in later frames it is near the pins/impacting them. A complete throw, score registration, transition to the next ball or frame, and loop repetition were not observed.
progress_feedback: The active-game frame shows the indicators FRAME 1/5, Ball 1, Total 0, Best 0, Max possible 150, Lane: no drift, and Guide 100%. No score change or frame progression was observed in the recorded frames; a change in the image alone does not prove input acceptance.
decisions_risk_reward: The page claims that aiming, power, and hook can be adjusted, but this recording cannot confirm effective decisions or actual risk/reward. The remaining pin state is visible in the frames, but its relationship to input selection or reward has not been proven.
rewards: The page and official card state a 150 maximum and a ranking table; in active gameplay, Total and Best are seen as 0. Successful scoring, a final reward, or rank advancement was not observed.
penalties_failure: No loss, error, gutter, penalty, or direct failure message was observed in the frames. The existence or rules of such a consequence are unclear.
outcomes_replay: The final outcome, win/loss, end of frame, or possibility of replay was not observed; therefore replay and loop repeatability are unclear.
onboarding: The opening page displays a Bowl button and a four-step guide for movement, aiming, power, and hook, and has Leaderboard, Settings, and language options. Successful onboarding or confirmation of all controls was not observed.
visual_audio_accessibility: The frames show a three-dimensional bowling environment with multiple lanes, neon colors, pins, a ball, a score HUD, and a pause button. On-screen text for status and controls is present. No reliable direct data about audio or accessibility options was observed; metadata records only an AudioContext warning.
technical_clues: A canvas with dimensions 1280×800 is recorded in the metadata; this is a technical clue and does not establish game behavior.
The metadata records 8 script, one stylesheet, 6 fetches, and Three.js/ WebGL indicators; no dedicated engine marker or tuning constant was recorded.
The AudioContext warning says that starting audio was not permitted after a user gesture; this concerns audio activation, not the absence of audio in the game design.
A WebGL software fallback warning and BufferGeometry/ShadowMap warnings were recorded; they are clues about the runtime environment and do not confirm mechanics.
A 403 error was recorded in the console, but page_errors and request_failures are empty; its effect on the game is unclear.
transferable_principles: Present the control tutorial in several short, readable steps before starting, but make acceptance of each input clear through real feedback.
Keep stage status, score, and remaining capacity stable in the HUD so the player can understand progress.
Do not separate continuous visual feedback from the mechanical result; a frame change alone should not be the only sign of success.
Show the action, result, and opportunity to repeat clearly so replay and skill learning can be identified.
candle_climber_relevance: For Candle Climber, keep score/rank dependent only on skill and gameplay execution, not on purchases or wallet and economic advantage.
From this sample, only the principle of a clear HUD and staged feedback is transferable; do not infer any specific control or path without direct testing.
Do not introduce free brake, horizontal direction change, or a branching path requiring new control; if such an option is considered, it is only a hypothesis requiring separate testing.
do_not_copy: Do not reproduce this game's name, text, visual identity, character, asset, or brand.
Do not copy its exact scene structure or layout and visual effects.
Do not treat the card's claim about 5 frames, a 150 maximum, or same lane as a confirmed, transferable mechanic.
Do not present a change across two frames or a generic input sequence as proof of controllability or game success.

evidence.claim: The opening frame shows an introductory page with a Bowl button, a movement/aiming/power/hook guide, and interface options.
The page text introduces these same four control categories and displays the phrase 5 frames and a 150 maximum; this text is an instruction/claim, not a successful control test.
The official game card claims 5 frames, 150 max, same lane, and the goal of getting a strike/perfect game; this claim was not confirmed by a complete playtest loop.
The active-game frame shows FRAME 1/5, Ball 1, Total 0, Best 0, Max possible 150, Lane: no drift, and Guide 100%.

In the after_combined_input and late frames, the ball and pins are seen in different states near the end of the lane; this visual change alone does not establish input acceptance or a scoring outcome.
The late frame still shows FRAME 1/5, Ball 1, and Total 0; the end of the loop or an outcome was not observed.
The metadata records a canvas with dimensions 1280×800, script/fetch resources, and Three.js/WebGL and AudioContext warnings; these are possible technical clues.

limitations: The recording covers only part of the game. Three frames, load, after_combined_input, and late, are from fallback-1, while two frames, after_start and after_key_burst, are current; timing and differences in origin may affect comparison. The metadata says that the load, after_combined_input, and late screenshots timed out, start_action was none, the generic inputs Space/ArrowUp/w/ArrowRight and holding ArrowRight+Space were tested, but no input acceptance signal was recorded. No web browsing or inference about hidden controls was performed.
